digest.component_or_area: completion verifier, budget sizing, verdict persistence
propositions: Verifier step budget exhausts on legitimate multi-criterion validation (epic with 6-14 ACs), misclassifying unproven criteria as unmet rather than budget-limited, driving false FAIL outcomes at request_limit 24-56.

Current formula (steps_per_criterion * c, clamped to 480) lacks evidence-surface scaling for child traversal and fixed overhead, underestimating epic-scope costs; raising defaults to 24/160 with clamp to 960 and adding child-traversal term (16 steps per direct child + 16 fixed overhead) sizes budgets correctly.

Re-verifying exhausted-run criteria re-proves all work without reusing prior PASS verdicts, consuming 10 min per cycle; a cross-run cache keyed by criterion-text hash and scoped git blob-SHA fingerprint (per file_impact paths, direct-child union for epics) persists validated PASS only, seeded into subsequent runs to skip redundant proof.

Cached PASS verdicts (seeded: true) are excluded from primary manifest and marked do-not-re-verify in the primary context; finalizer downgrades and omissions on seeded records are replaced by the cached bank record, while same-run downgrades remain preserved.

Fingerprint validity must bind to the verification target ref (not HEAD), so verdicts proven against a pinned commit ref store verified_ref_sha and load only when the current run targets the same ref, preventing false reuse across unrelated commits.
Runaway guards (tool_calls_limit, loop detection) remain unchanged and authoritative; the step budget exists solely for preventing runaway tool use, never as an artificial validation cap.
